title: Internal traffic multiplexer Terraform module: SNI proxy, per-service TLS, and certificate rotation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: Build a reusable Terraform module that acts as an internal traffic multiplexer for Private (VPC) Redwood deployments. The module will provide a configurable SNI-based proxy in front of internal services, support per-service TLS termination or passthrough, automated certificate rotation via KMS/HSM-compatible flows, and dynamic health probe translation for heterogeneous backends.

Scope:
- Terraform module that provisions an internal NLB for TCP-level routing and an ALB (or ALB-compatible proxy layer) for HTTP/S SNI termination when required.
- Support for per-service target groups created from service tags or a module input map.
- Certificate rotation path: integrate with customer KMS or Redwood-managed certs, with blue/green rotation and zero-downtime rebind.
- Health check translation: allow per-service probe rewrite rules (path, host header, expected HTTP codes) and transparent TCP/HTTP fallback.
- Connection draining and graceful failover between target groups during rolling upgrades.
- IAM least-privilege policy templates for operators and automation to run within customer Private control plane.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Module supports three deploy modes via variable: "nlb-only", "nlb-with-alb-proxy", and "alb-public-edges" (internal-only semantics).
2) Per-service TLS toggle: tls_mode = ["passthrough", "terminate", "sni-routed"].
3) Cert rotation can be initiated by a Terraform variable (rotation_trigger) or via a lightweight external automation that updates an SSM/Secrets entry; rotation must not drop >0.5% of requests in a 5m window in our load tests.
4) Health checks configurable per-target-group, with rewrite templates and a fallback to TCP probe for legacy handlers.
5) Automated test harness with local terraform + kic/localstack tests and an integration test harness in CI that exercises canary rollout and drain behavior.
6) Docs: module README, upgrade notes for existing customers, migration script to convert current NLB+ALB stacks into module-managed stacks without downtime.

Design notes & trade-offs:
- We intentionally separate TCP and HTTP layers to keep NLB for high-throughput passthrough and ALB for SNI termination where L7 features are required; customers can pick levels of complexity.
- To avoid complex cross-account certs, KMS integration will start with a managed-secrets approach and an operator-run job for HSM-backed rotations. Full HSM automation is out-of-scope for the first pass.
- We will prefer target group creation via explicit map inputs (service_name -> { port, health, tls_mode }) to keep the module deterministic; an optional tag discovery mode exists but is beta.
- Backward compatibility: provide a migration plan that creates parallel target groups and switches routing in a phased canary by tag.

Terraform interface (high level):
- Inputs (examples): vpc_id, private_subnets, mode, services_map (map of objects), rotation_trigger, kms_key_arn, enable_metrics, monitoring_sns_topic.
- Outputs (examples): ingress_dns, target_group_arns, active_cert_arn, module_version_tag.

Observability & SLOs:
- Emit metrics to CloudWatch/prometheus for TLS handshake errors, 4xx/5xx rate by service, unhealthy target counts, and certificate expiry days.
- Add an optional tracing header passthrough to help correlate probe failures to application traces.

Upgrade and rollout plan:
1) Create module in experimental namespace; test with non-prod VPC.
2) Run migration tool on staging customer environments; validate zero-drop canary at 5% traffic for 30m.
3) Promote to GA and schedule for existing Private customers via support-run migration (automated script + dry-run output).

Security considerations:
- Limit IAM used by Terraform to manage load balancers and cert storage; avoid exposing KMS keys to module consumers.
- All secrets referenced by the module must be marked as "sensitive" in Terraform and stored in customer-managed secret store.
- Module should enable audit logging for ALB access logs and CloudWatch ACLs.

Acceptance tests & QA:
- Unit tests for Terraform plan diffs produced by the module given common inputs.
- Integration tests that spin up small EC2 targets with health endpoints and validate probe rewrites and TLS rotations.
- Chaos test to simulate target termination and ensure connection draining keeps errors below the SLO.

Links & artifacts:
- RFC (Confluence): https://confluence.internal.redwood/PrivateIngressMultiplexerRFC (draft)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1824 (WIP)
- Migration script: https://gitlab.redwood/private-deploy/migrate-nlb-to-multiplexer (alpha)

Notes: This ticket encapsulates module design and core implementation. Follow-up tickets will split out the operator automation, full HSM rotation, and the tag-discovery beta mode.
